title: Personal e-banking transfer/remittance tariff (跨境汇款电汇)
proposition: Cross-border wire: 1‰ of the amount, min CNY 50, max CNY 260 per wire, plus cable fee CNY 150 outside HK/Macau/Taiwan. Standard since 2014-11-01; note 1: agreements, discounts and local differences can apply.

title: Notice adjusting personal service charges (effective 2026-11-11) — overseas ATM withdrawal
proposition: Overseas and HK/Macau/Taiwan ATM withdrawal, UnionPay: CNY 12 + 1% of the amount per withdrawal, max CNY 112; Mastercard/VISA: 2.5%, min USD 3, max USD 40.

title: 2026 personal-FX Q&A (08): foreign individual's work income, 2026-07-13
proposition: 汇发〔2020〕14号 Art. 59: a foreign individual (境外个人) buying FX from lawful current-account RMB income earned in China presents ID plus source-of-funds materials with transaction amounts (including tax evidence).

title: 2024 current-account FX Q&A case (09), 2024-06-21
proposition: Same Art. 59, plus: only a foreign individual holding the Foreign Permanent Resident ID (外国人永久居留身份证) gets the annual convenience amount for FX purchases.

title: 2022 FX policy Q&A (08), 2022-09-29
proposition: Arts. 54-57: personal FX settlement and domestic individuals' FX purchases use a USD 50,000 per person per year convenience amount; it is not an annual limit — above it, ID alone is not enough and source/purpose materials with transaction amounts are required; genuine lawful current-account and opened capital-account items have no amount limit.

issuer: NPC (text on State Taxation Administration site)
title: PRC Individual Income Tax Law (2018 amendment)
proposition: Art. 2: nine taxable categories (inheritance is not listed). Art. 3: comprehensive income 3%-45% progressive; business income 5%-35%; interest/dividends, property rent, property transfer and incidental income 20% flat. Art. 6(5): property-transfer income = proceeds minus original value and reasonable costs. Art. 13: if the payer did not withhold, the taxpayer pays.

title: Foreign Exchange Regulation (State Council Decree 532)
proposition: Art. 5: the State does not restrict recurring international payments and transfers. Art. 12: genuine lawful transaction basis. Art. 39 (capital flight 逃汇) and Art. 40 (illegal FX purchase 套汇): fine up to 30% of the amount, 30%-100% in serious cases, criminal liability possible. Art. 42 (carrying FX in breach): warning, fine up to 20%. Art. 45 (private FX trading): warning, confiscation, fine up to 30%, 30%-100% serious. Art. 48: untrue documents, individual fine up to CNY 50,000. Art. 52(2): 境内个人 includes a foreigner resident in China for one continuous year.

title: 2026 personal-FX Q&A (10): changing back unused RMB, 2026-09-17
proposition: Art. 60: a foreign individual may change back unused RMB with ID and the original exchange slip (兑换水单); the slip is valid 24 months from the exchange date. Up to USD 500 equivalent per day (USD 1,000 at departure venues outside customs) on ID alone.

title: Notice on overseas card cash withdrawals, 汇发〔2017〕29号
proposition: All cards in one person's name combined: max CNY 100,000 equivalent per calendar year overseas cash withdrawal; over the cap, withdrawals are suspended for that year and the next. Per card per day max CNY 10,000 equivalent. Borrowing/lending cards to evade is prohibited.

title: Q&A: how much foreign-currency cash may be carried out each time, 2019-05-21
proposition: Up to USD 5,000 equivalent: customs releases directly. USD 5,000-10,000: bank-issued carrying permit (携带外汇出境许可证) required. Above USD 10,000: SAFE permit, in principle not granted except special cases.

title: Comparison of Form 8938 and FBAR requirements
proposition: FBAR: file if aggregate foreign accounts exceed USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year; due Apr 15, automatic extension to Oct 15. Form 8938 (living in US): unmarried >USD 50,000 last day / >USD 75,000 any time; joint double; living abroad: unmarried USD 200,000/300,000, joint USD 400,000/600,000. Form 8938 penalty up to USD 10,000 plus USD 10,000 per 30 days after IRS notice, max USD 60,000. Form 8938 does not replace the FBAR.

title: United States–PRC Income Tax Convention (treaty PDF), Art. 9
proposition: Art. 9(2): dividends paid by a company resident in one State to a beneficial owner resident in the other State may be taxed in the paying State, but the tax charged shall not exceed 10% of the gross dividends. (Eligibility procedure not verified in this pass — flag F52-U06.)

title: 31 CFR 1010.821 penalty adjustment table (up to date as of 11/09/2026)
proposition: For penalties assessed on or after Jan 17, 2025: non-willful FBAR violation (31 USC 5321(a)(5)(B)(i)) max USD 16,536; willful violation (5321(a)(5)(C)(i)(I)) USD 165,353. eCFR is authoritative but unofficial (see flag F52-U10).

title: Yearly average currency exchange rates
proposition: China Yuan per USD: 2025 7.129; 2024 7.189; 2023 7.075. 'The Internal Revenue Service has no official exchange rate.' A taxpayer may need to recognise foreign-currency gain or loss under IRC §988.

title: Gifts from a foreign person (Form 3520)
proposition: Report gifts/bequests from a nonresident alien or foreign estate on Form 3520 Part IV only if the aggregate from that person (and related persons) exceeds USD 100,000 in the tax year; each gift over USD 5,000 is then identified separately. Foreign-corporation/partnership threshold: USD 20,573 for 2026.

title: Instructions for Form 3520 (12/2025) — penalties
proposition: Failure to report a §6039F foreign gift on time: penalty 5% of the gift amount per month the failure continues, max 25%; the IRS may also determine the income-tax consequences of the gift. Reasonable-cause exception applies.

issuer: U.S. Government Publishing Office / Cornell LII text of 26 USC 988
title: 26 U.S.C. §988 — treatment of certain foreign currency transactions
proposition: §988(a)(1)(A): foreign-currency gain/loss on a §988 transaction is ordinary. Disposition of nonfunctional currency is a §988 transaction. §988(e): no gain is recognised on an individual's personal transaction unless the gain exceeds USD 200; a transaction is not personal to the extent its expenses fall under §162/§212. Character conflict with IRS Pub. 525 — flag F52-U05.

title: Publication 525 — foreign currency transactions
proposition: Plain-language summary: gain on a personal foreign-currency transaction is not included in income unless it is more than USD 200; if more, Pub. 525 says to report it as a capital gain. (Conflicts with §988(a) ordinary treatment — flag F52-U05; do not rely on either without advice.)

title: 汇发〔2015〕?? watch-list (关注名单) management for evading quota/authenticity controls
proposition: Borrowing or lending one's convenience amount to evade amount/authenticity controls puts the person on the watch list for the year of listing and the following two consecutive years; during that period FX business needs ID plus transaction-amount materials under strict authenticity review.
